# IG Parameters

Baseline: hl7.fhir.uv.tools 1.3.0, IG Publisher 3.0.4, fhir.base.template 1.0.0.
Sources: TOOLS-1.3.0, IGPUB-3.0.4, TPL-BASE-1.0.0

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_ig_parameters.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every code in the FHIR Tooling IG's `ig-parameters` CodeSystem, with what two other layers do with it.
The three columns answer different questions, so a disagreement between them is a finding, not an error
to settle by rank:

- **Publisher reads**: the code has a `case` in the IG parameter `switch` of `PublisherIGLoader.java` at
  3.0.4 (lines 450-977) [src: IGPUB-3.0.4 org.hl7.fhir.publisher.core/…/PublisherIGLoader.java:450-977].
  "no" means only that this `switch` doesn't handle it: other classes may still read the code, and an
  unhandled code that isn't a template parameter is recorded as unknown (`pf.unknownParams`).
- **Template parameter**: the code is listed in `template-parameters` in fhir.base.template 1.0.0's
  `config.json`, so the publisher passes it through to the template instead of treating it as unknown.
- **Base template default**: fhir.base.template 1.0.0's `onLoad.xslt` adds this parameter to every IG
  built on it. *Added alongside* means the default is added even when the IG sets its own value; *only if
  unset* means the IG's value replaces it.

## Definitions

Verbatim from `CodeSystem.concept.definition`, `http://hl7.org/fhir/tools/CodeSystem/ig-parameters` version 1.3.0.

### logging

Display: logging [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#logging]

```text
Which kinds of log output messages to produce - the value is a code, from this list:

* ```init```: Messages describing the start up process (for debugging)
* ```progress```: Overall progress messages
* ```tx```: Messages describing the use of the terminology server (for debugging)
* ```generate```: Log when producing an individual resource  (troubleshooting only - leave off)
* ```html```: Log when validating an html page (troubleshooting only - leave off)
* ```template```: see template log output
```

### generate

Display: generate [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#generate]

```text
Fine grained control over generation of resources:

* ```example-narratives```: generate narrative in examples if they don't have any (as opposed to conformance resources, which are always generated)
* ```genExamples```: produce extra examples (todo: document this)

Except: you can't turn example-narratives off. Todo: decide why this exists. But you can suppress - see next item
```

### no-narrative

Display: no-narrative [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-narrative]

```text
A resource to suppress narrative generation for (and Resource.text will be removed if found). Format is ```(type)/(id)``` e.g. ```Patient/example```, or type or id may be ```*``` e.g. ```Task/*``` - do not generate narrative for any Task resource.

Narrative Generation should never be suppressed for any canonical resource

Note for HL7 users: the FMG will review which resources have narrative suppressed and why when publication approval is sought
```

### no-validate

Display: no-validate [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-validate]

```text
A resource not to validate. Format is ```(type)/(id)``` e.g. ```Patient/example```, or type or id may be ```*``` e.g. ```Task/*``` - do not validate any Task resource.

Suppressing validation is generally a bad idea. There's two contexts where it might be useful: validation of really big resources that takes a long time, and examples that are purposefully wrong to demonstrate what not to do. But while it sounds good - don't bother me with problems I mean to introduce, it's too easy for other unintended problems to accumulate. So it's better to keep validation on.

ote for HL7 users: the FMG will review which resources have validation suppressed and why when publication approval is sought. FMG would generally prefer to see explicit errors for resources that are wrong intentionally, and will OK publication in this case. **It's going to reviewed either way.**
```

Display: no-check-usage [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-check-usage]

```text
Do not check usage for extensions and data types - for IGs where they are being defined for use elsewhere
```

The trade-off is that conformance statement rendering (which requires terminology) will not work when this is set, so only set it for IGs that do not use conformance statements.

### propagate-status

Display: propagate-status [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#propagate-status]

```text
If true, indicates that the FMM and Standards Status declarations from top-level artifacts should be propagated to any dependencies that don't declare their own values.  If different statuses or maturity level would propagate to a dependency from different artifacts, the 'highest' FMM or most mature standards status will apply (Normative or Informative, then STU, then Draft).  Information does not propagate to artifacts marked as examples or as experimental.
Propagation is based on references.  E.g. the IG references everything (so its status will propagate everywhere by default).  If there are higher statuses on certain CapabilityStatements, Operations or Profiles, those status will propagate to the artifacts they reference, such as other profiles, ValueSets or CodeSystems.
Propagation only happens within the context of an IG.  There is no propagation across artifacts present in other IG packages listed as dependencies.
```

### validation

Display: validation [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#validation]

```text
Fine grained control over validation flags when validating resources / IGs:

* ```check-must-support```: Does nothing! (for now?)
* ```allow-any-extensions```: Allow any extensions at all (and therefore miss accidental broken extension references)
* ```check-aggregation```: check that aggregation is correct (in IGs, bundles are often broken up for publishing / documentation purposes)
* ```no-broken-links```: forbid broken links in HTML pages - stop the build if any are found
* ```show-reference-messages```: when validating, instead of showing a summary of issues from validating the target of references, just show all the validation messages in detail
* ```no-experimental-content```: create an error if the IG contains any experimental content
```

### generate-version

Display: generate-version [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#generate-version]

```text
Request that the IG publisher generate packages for additional versions than the stated version e.g. the IG might be for authored against version 4.0, but also produce an R3 version.

For each occurence of this parameter, the IG publisher will produce an extra package, with the filename id.ver.tgz where id is the main id of the ig, and ver is the parameter value. (note that this is different to the main package which is always called package.tgz). 

This parameter can have one one of following values:

* r2
* r2b
* r3
* r4
* r5

This parameter should be used with great care, and only after consulting the FHIR Product director to consider all of it's ramifications. It's generally only appropriate for terminology resources.
 It's not an error to generate the same version as the IG itself - this is typically done for consistency of use across versions
```

```text
Note: see [Patterns for Formatting and Parsing](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/format/DateTimeFormatter.html) for Java String formats
```

### no-modifiers

Display: no-modifiers [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-modifiers]

```text
If set to ```true```, it means that all profiles created within the implementation guide will have their differential modified to set maxOccurs=0 on all ```isModifier``` elements that are not explicitly mentioned in the original source differential.
```

### jekyll-timeout

Display: jekyll-timeout [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#jekyll-timeout]

```text
How long to let Jekyll run before giving up on it (seconds)
```

### suppressed-ids

Display: suppressed-ids [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#suppressed-ids]

```text
A comma separated list of resource ids to suppress ids when they are rendered in the Implementation Guide.

This is useful because the IG publication process requires all resources to have ids, so they can be handled. But in some Implementation Guides, some examples should not have ids .e.g showing an example of posting a new resource. If the resource is listed here, the id will be removed in the publication (but not the package, where the resources must have ids).
The format is either type/id, or just id. Repeating parameters just add more to the list. If the parameter is present with the special value $examples, then all examples will have ids suppressed
If the parameter is not present, then all resources will have ids.
```

### tabbed-snapshots

Display: tabbed-snapshots [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#tabbed-snapshots]

```text
A boolean that indicates that the implementation guide leverages tabs to include alternate dictionary views and that tabs for differential, key and/or must-support tables should link to anchors specific to those tables rather than only to the default 'snapshot' keys.
```

### jira-code

Display: jira-code [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#jira-code]

```text
If your IG is published via HL7 and should your package ID diverge from the file name in the JIRA-Spec-Artifacts repository, this parameter will help point to the right file.
```

Display: r4-exclusion [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#r4-exclusion]

```text
For an R4B IG, ignore this profile when considering conversion to R4, or for an R4 IG, omit this when generating the R4 specific package. Value is either '{type}/{id}' or '{url}'
```

### r4b-exclusion

```text
For an R4 IG, ignore this resource when considering conversion to R4B, or for an R4B IG, omit this when generating the R4B specific package. Value is either '{type}/{id}' or '{url}'
```

```text
When generating an R4-specific package, include this resource. Do not include this resource in packages for any other FHIR versions. Value is either '{type}/{id}' or '{url}'
```

### r4b-inclusion

Display: r4b-inclusion [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#r4b-inclusion]

```text
When generating an R4B-specific package, include this resource. Do not include this resource in packages for any other FHIR versions. Value is either '{type}/{id}' or '{url}'
```

```text
When generating an R5-specific package, include this resource. Do not include this resource in packages for any other FHIR versions. Value is either '{type}/{id}' or '{url}'
```

```text
When generating an R6-specific package, include this resource. Do not include this resource in packages for any other FHIR versions. Value is either '{type}/{id}' or '{url}'
```

```text
Produce the resources as .json in the jekyll _data folder. Note that Jekyll will fail if any of the resources contain non-ascii characters
```

Display: page-factory [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#page-factory]

```text
Reference to a [Page Factory](page-factories.html)
```

Display: globals-in-artifacts [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#globals-in-artifacts]

```text
If true, causes the list of global profiles to appear at the top of the Artifacts Summary page
```

```text
If true, causes the terminology parameters list to appear at the top of the Artifacts Summary page
```

Display: No root table-of-contents [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#noRootToc]

```text
If true, causes the ig to not inject a root 'toc' page if that's not already the root (only functions in templates that do this by default)
```

### artifactsOnRoot

Display: Artifacts on root [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#artifactsOnRoot]

```text
If true, causes artifact pages to be created as children of the IG's 'root' page rather than the 'artifacts' page (if the template supports doing that)
```

### conversion-version

Display: conversion-version [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#conversion-version]

```text
Defines an additional version of the FHIR definitions to load for version conversion maps. Value is either RX or V.V (e.g. R4 or 4.0). Additional versions are loaded with modified URLs (e.g. R4 is loaded to http://hl7.org.fhir/4.0)
```

### no-usage-check

Display: no-usage-check [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-usage-check]

```text
No Warning in QA if there are extensions/profiles that are not used in this IG
```

### i18n-default-lang

Display: i18n-default-lang [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#i18n-default-lang]

```text
The default language (e.g. [[[Resource.language]]]) to assume in the IG when the resource and/or the element context doesn't specify a language
```

### i18n-lang

Display: i18n-lang [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#i18n-lang]

```text
A language to translate the IG into as any valid language code (mostly a 2 letter language code, or combination language + region) (e.g. `fr`, `nl`, `de`). Note that i18n-default-lang is automatically a language, and doesn't need to be restated
```

### translation-sources

Display: translation-sources [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#translation-sources]

```text
A folder in which to look for translation source files - .po or .xliff or .json
```

### translation-supplements

Display: translation-supplements [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#translation-supplements]

```text
A folder in which to look for translation supplements - .po or .xliff or .json. This is deprecated - use translation-sources instead
```

### display-warnings

Display: display-warnings [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#display-warnings]

```text
Instruct the terminology layer that wrong displays result in a warning not an error. Note that you have to clear the terminology cache manually when changing the value of this parameter.
```

### logged-when-scanning

Display: logged-when-scanning [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#logged-when-scanning]

```text
Whether to report issues when scanning files for resources. Valid values are: true, false, stack
```

### validation-duration-report-cutoff

Display: validation-duration-report-cutoff [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#validation-duration-report-cutoff]

```text
An integer value that specifies the a number of seconds. If any resource takes longer than that time, it will be reported in the log
```

### viewDefinition

Display: viewDefinition [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#viewDefinition]

```text
A ViewDefinition to execute (path to file). Output is added in the package.db file as a generated table, and can be used in the page contents. See also [documentation](https://build.fhir.org/ig/FHIR/ig-guidance/sql.html)
```

### fixed-value-format

Display: Fixed Value Format Code [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#fixed-value-format]

```text
A code that indicates how to format fixed and pattern values. Valid values for this parameter are json | json-all | xml | all-xml. The -all options relate to primitives - whether they are shown just as a value or as a formatted fragment
```

### auto-oid-root

Display: OID root for automatically assigned OIDs [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#auto-oid-root]

```text
Defines the OID root for the IG. Must be globally unique. see OIDs are easy to assign - see https://build.fhir.org/ig/FHIR/ig-guidance/oids.html. If this is present, any canonical resources that do not have OIDs assigned manually will have OIDs automatically assigned by the publisher. The OID assignments are stored in oids.ini next to the IG resource for the IG, and must be committed with other changes to the source.
```

### test-data-factories

Display: Generate a set of instances for testing from a spreadsheet [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#test-data-factories]

```text
Prompts the Publisher to generate a set of instances for testing given a json file as described here: <https://build.fhir.org/ig/FHIR/ig-guidance/testfactory.html>
```

### incubator-ig

Display: Use the generated code for an incubator IG [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#incubator-ig]

```text
Identifies an incubator IG whose resources this IG works with. The value is a code from the list of incubator IGs for which code has been generated into the publisher (see the allowed values). When this parameter is present, the publisher uses the incubator IG's definitions of its resources in place of the definitions in the base specification. Codes currently supported: `hl7.fhir.uv.testing` - the FHIR Testing IG (TestPlan, TestScript, TestReport)
```

### resource-language-policy

Display: Control Automatic population of Resource.language: all-ig | ig-realm | all-realm [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#resource-language-policy]

```text
Controls how the IG Publisher populates Resource.language. Missing = do nothing. 'all-ig' = populate all resources with what's in the ig. 'ig-realm' = populate just the IG with the language implied by the realm. 'all-realm' - populated all the resources with the language implied by the realm
```

### profile-test-cases

Display: Profile test cases [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#profile-test-cases]

```text
A file that contains a set of profile test cases
```

### related-ig

Display: related-ig [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#related-ig]

```text
Defines a related IG - an IG that depends on this IG that is developed with it. Format is `role:code=id` - see [Related IGs](https://build.fhir.org/ig/FHIR/ig-guidance/branches/master/related-igs.html) for further information
```

### pin-canonicals

Display: Pin Canonical Versions [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#pin-canonicals]

```text
Defines how the IG publisher treats unversioned canonical references. Possible values:

* `pin-none`: no action is taken (default)
* `pin-all`: any unversioned canonical references that can be resolved through the package dependencies will have |(version) appended to the canonical, where (version) is the latest available within the package dependencies
* `pin-multiples`: pinning the canonical reference will only happen if there is multiple versions found in the package dependencies
```

### pin-manifest

Display: Manifest to use when pinning [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#pin-manifest]

```text
If this parameter is present, then pinning is redirected to a manifest rather than being performed on the canonical reference itself. The value is the ID of a parameters resource
```

### r5-bundle-relative-reference-policy

Display: R5 Bundle Relative Reference Policy [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#r5-bundle-relative-reference-policy]

```text
Defines when the validation engine in the publisher applies the revised resolution for relative reference as described in the R5 specification. Possible values:

* `default`: apply in R5+ (default)
* `never`: never apply the revised algorithm 
* `always`: the new algorithm is applied irrespective of the version of the IG
```

### generate-uml

Display: Generate UML Setting [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#generate-uml]

```text
Control whether UML Diagrams are generated for StructureDefinitions.. Possible values:

* `none`: Do not generate any UML (default)
* `source`: generate when a source diagram is found 
* `all`: Generate a UML diagram always
```

### page-heading-level

Display: page-heading-level [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#page-heading-level]

```text
The heading level that the top heading of every generated page is moved to. When this is set, the HTML checks shift the headings on each page so that its top heading sits at this level, keeping the structure beneath it; pages that have more than one top level heading are left alone and reported instead. When it is not set, heading levels are left exactly as generated.

Only set this if your template's CSS has been written for it: templates that number headings with CSS counters keyed to h2/h3/h4 will number pages wrongly if the headings move underneath them
```

### accessibility-checks

Display: accessibility-checks [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#accessibility-checks]

```text
Whether the HTML checks look for the accessibility problems that can be found in the generated markup (warnings with ids starting HTML_A11Y_): images without alternative text, form controls without labels, links with no text or text like 'click here', click handlers on things a keyboard cannot reach, aria attributes that refer to ids that are not on the page, frames without titles, pages without titles, and so on. These are based on the parts of the HHS Section 508 checklist (WCAG) that can be tested without a browser. They are off by default: set this to true to turn them on. When they are on, local builds also get an accessibility check panel at the bottom of each page, which runs a fuller check (including colour contrast) in the browser. It does not affect the other HTML checks, including the heading structure and page language checks
```

### narrative-heading-level

Display: narrative-heading-level [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#narrative-heading-level]

```text
The heading level that a resource's narrative is placed at when it is rendered into a page. The headings in the narrative - whether the author wrote them or a renderer generated them - are shifted so that the highest one sits at this level, preserving the structure beneath it. The default of 3 suits templates that title a page with an h2; set this if your template titles pages at a different level. If the narrative is nested too deeply to shift (it would need a heading below h6) it is left alone, and reported by the HTML checks instead
```

### no-cibuild-issues

Display: Suppress CIBuild Warnings [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-cibuild-issues]

```text
For integrity and security reasons, the ci-build enforces some requirements about the generated HTML, and the IG publisher gives warnings about these for all IGs. This parameter is used to turn those warnings, for IGs that will never be on the ci-build
```

### suppress-mappings

Display: Suppress an inherited mapping [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#suppress-mappings]

```text
By default, snapshots inherit mappings, and the mappings are carried through. But many of them aren't useful, or desired, and can be suppressed by adding this parameter. The value is the URI found in StructureDefinition.mapping.uri. The special value '*' suppresses most of the mappings in the main specification
```

Display: Want to generate JSON [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#wantGen-json]

```text
Allows overriding to prohibit generating JSON files
```

### wantGen-json-html

Display: Want to generate JSON HTML [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#wantGen-json-html]

```text
Allows overriding to prohibit generating JSON HTML files
```

### wantGen-ttl

Display: Want to generate TTL [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#wantGen-ttl]

```text
Allows overriding to prohibit generating TTL files
```

### wantGen-ttl-html

Display: Want to generate TTL HTML [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#wantGen-ttl-html]

```text
Allows overriding to prohibit generating TTL HTML files
```

### wantGen-xml

Display: Want to generate XML [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#wantGen-xml]

```text
Allows overriding to prohibit generating XML files
```

### wantGen-xml-html

Display: Want to generate XML HTML [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#wantGen-xml-html]

```text
Allows overriding to prohibit generating XML HTML files
```

### no-xig-link

Display: Suppress XIG link [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-xig-link]

```text
Suppresses the XIG link that automatically appears on extensions - for IGs that do not find their way into the Cross-IG statistics analysis (which covers all public/published IGs)
```

### no-expansions-files

Display: Suppress Generation of Expansions files [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-expansions-files]

```text
Suppresses the generation of expansions files, typically for performance reasons on structural IGs. Note that this needs to have template support, since some templates put these in the downloads automatically
```

### no-ig-database

Display: Suppress Generation of Expansions files [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#no-ig-database]

```text
Suppresses the generation of the database file for the IG - typically for performance reasons
```

### additional-resource

Display: Additional Resource Name [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#additional-resource]

```text
Defines an additional resource that this IG will publish. The value is a file reference to the StructureDefinition that defines the resource. This requires additional steps - see [Defining Additional Resources](https://build.fhir.org/resource.html#additional)
```

### toggle-changes

Display: Toggle Text Changes [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#toggle-changes]

```text
If true causes rendering of text changes to default to 'on'.  If false, causes rendering of text changes to default to off
```

### strict-identifiers

Display: Strict Identifier Systems [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#strict-identifiers]

```text
If true, will give info messages if non-example identifier systems are present that aren't preferred URIs in known NamingSystems
```

### dataset

Display: dataset [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#dataset]

```text
A relative path to a set of resources to load as a data set. Datasets are rendered differently from regular resources in the IG - see [todo].
```

### ig-expansion-parameters

Display: ig-expansion-parameters [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#ig-expansion-parameters]

```text
Specifies where an IG consumer can find the expansion parameters used during the creation of the IG. The usual (but ony only) use for this is to specify the applicable SNOMED CT edition
```

### custom-resource

Display: custom-resource [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#custom-resource]

```text
Defines a custom resource type that this IG uses. The value is a file reference to the StructureDefinition that defines the custom resource. Unlike additional-resource, custom resources are not published by this IG but are used within it.
```

### language-translations-mode

Display: Language Translations Mode [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#language-translations-mode]

```text
Controls how language translations are handled in resources for the language specific rendering of a multi-language IG. By default, instances will only include the value for the relevant language. If the value of this parameter is 'preserve', then all the translations will be retained; they'll be reorganized so that the relevant language is the primary value.
```

### requirements-category-vs

Display: Requirements Category Value Set [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#requirements-category-vs]

```text
Indicates the canonical of the value set from which requirements category codes are drawn when they appear inline as part of conformance statement markup
```

### lang-pack

Display: Language Pack [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#lang-pack]

```text
Indicates that the IG creates a language pack, and the CodeSystems should be marked accordingly
```

### wcag-conformant

Display: WCAG Conformant [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#wcag-conformant]

```text
Indicates that the IG should be WCAG Conformant (or at least, more conformant). Note that WCAG compliance reduces the rendering freedom, and the resulting content is harder to read for the majority of readers. Where there's no reduction in utility, the content is already WCAG conformant
```

### infer-resource-conformance

Display: Infer Resource Conformance [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#infer-resource-conformance]

```text
If true, indicates that the conformance level for a resource in a CapabilityStatement will be inferred based on the maximum conformance expectation of interactions and search parameters used within the resource
```

### signatures-using-r6-method

Display: Signatures Use R6 Method [src: TOOLS-1.3.0 CodeSystem-ig-parameters.json#signatures-using-r6-method]

```text
The way signatures are done on Bundles changed with R6. That method can be preadopted for signing bundles using this parameter (it is mandatory in R6)
```
